steps.text: Out of the fridge: Sunday's roast chicken and Sunday's rice-and-cauliflower — this lunch takes 175 g of chicken (her 75 g / him 100 g) from Sunday's 600 g batch.
Chicken (75/100 g) chopped into rough 2 cm pieces.

Pan, medium-high, rapeseed oil (her 6 g / him 8 g) — hits the hot pan, so it's the rapeseed portion per D0-003. Chicken in with ½ tsp oregano, ½ tsp cumin, ¼ tsp turmeric and salt. 3 minutes, moving it, until the edges catch.
Rice and cauliflower (55/80 g dry cooked + 130/160 g riced) warmed through — 90 seconds in the microwave, or into the pan for the last minute with a splash of water.

Build: rice base, chicken over, then chickpeas (70/90 g), shredded sweetheart cabbage (70/80 g — swapped for little gem per D0-003, it's shredded here) and diced tomato (80/100 g) around the edge. Raw red onion (30/40 g) over.
White sauce from Sunday's jar (50/65 g yoghurt, grated garlic, lemon, a great deal of black pepper). Hot sauce to taste.

why: The spices go on in the pan, not on Sunday. One tray of deliberately plain roast chicken becomes three completely different lunches this week precisely because it was left neutral.
notes: L5: takes 175 g of chicken from Sunday's 600 g roast-chicken batch (prep-a's 'Roast chicken' yield). The other two consumers (a-d3l, a-d5l) aren't in this fixture set, so the aggregate 175+?+?=575-with-25g-headroom check (D0-020) can't be evaluated here — lintL5Aggregate correctly withholds a verdict until all three have rewrites.
D0-003 applied twice in this card: oil into the hot pan becomes rapeseed_oil (6/8 g); the little gem is used shredded in the build step, so it becomes sweetheart_cabbage (70/80 g).
